Sidecar names follow the symlink, by two independent code paths that must agree. A port that names either sidecar from the configured path leaves an extra file the runner records as a delta. The symlink itself survives the write and still points at the same target.

The lock sidecar's mode does NOT follow the store's: `Store#with_lock` opens the lock file with a literal `0o644`, so a deliberately private 0600 store (`valid/restricted-mode-store`) acquires a world-readable sidecar. The lock file is empty, so only its existence and mtime leak. Recorded as Ruby's behavior, not fixed — a port that carries the store's mode onto the lock would be tidier and would diverge.

A PORT MUST NOT QUOTE `%L`/`%X`/`%Y` in the configured driver command string. Git pre-quotes those labels in the sequencer path — rebase and cherry-pick pass `'a1b2c3 (ours)'` already quoted — so wrapping them again produces `''a1b2c3 (ours)''`, a shell syntax error. The driver then never runs at all and git silently falls back to its own line-based text merge on tasks.jsonl, which is the exact outcome this driver exists to prevent. The failure is invisible to `git merge`, which passes either way: it is only reachable by driving rebase or cherry-pick, which is why both are now in the oracle. All three arguments are optional (arity 4..7) so installs carrying the older four-argument string keep working, falling back to marker width 7 and the labels ours/theirs.

notes: This is the capability users install into their own repos, so its failure mode is other people's data. Cancellation is timing-dependent by construction: #test_async_agent_cancellation_escalates_when_child_ignores_term asserts that a TERM-ignoring child is killed in under one wall-clock second, against CANCEL_TERM_GRACE + CANCEL_KILL_GRACE = 0.30s of budget.
